MAJOR: Unknown-field allowlists are hardcoded independently (Python `ContractSpec` fields vs Go `eventContractFields`) with only static, duplicated fixtures on each side; a field added to one language only passes every added test, so the design failure case "Python/Go shape mismatch → parity test fails CI" (CONTRACT_PARITY_MISMATCH) is not actually enforced for field-set drift.

Binding design parity coverage is incomplete: open-question resolutions require parity tests for cursor ordering (seq-only) and unknown envelope version — neither side has them; Python also lacks the subscription/alert-rule/webhook unknown-field tests that Go adds (`test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`).

Go `eventContractFields["subscription"]` (and `alert-rule`) omits `tenant_id`, while the design/guardrails require tenant fields in the subscription contract — a tenant-scoped subscription accepted by Python would be rejected by Go, an untested cross-language shape break on a security-relevant field.

Design obliges this item to define the contract metric names/labels (`contract_validation_failures_total{code}`, `contract_parity_test_failures`, owner platform+CI); the diff defines none, leaving BI-PF-1270/1274 without the promised contract.
MINOR: `WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF` is not declared in `core/contracts.py`, though spec_pack cites that file as its evidence (startup fail-closed validation is BI-PF-1270's, but the contract name belongs here).

FR-2 acceptance ("signature and event_id idempotency headers are present") is only half-tested: no assertion that `X-PF-Idempotency-Key` equals `event_id`; header constants are checked by tautological equality.
Go mirror defines no `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER`/`WEBHOOK_IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER` constants, so the header-name contract exists only in Python — an avoidable parity surface.

`webhook_signature`/`verify_webhook_signature` accept an empty secret and still produce/verify signatures; fail-closed at the primitive would be cheaper than relying solely on BI-PF-1270 startup checks (CL-013 posture).
NIT: Added test names diverge from the design test_matrix names (`test_contracts_unknown_field_parity`, `test_contracts_seq_parity`, `test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`), weakening traceability evidence for FR-1/FR-2.
New file `go/pfcore/event_contracts_test.go` is not in the declared `affected_files`.
Go `containsField` is a linear scan over a fixed allowlist; a set/map lookup would be idiomatic and O(1) — negligible at this size.
SUMMARY: Additive, reversible contract work that stays within the approved file scope and language guardrails, and the added tests plausibly satisfy the literal AC (tests pass), but parity is fixture-based rather than cross-checked, so Python/Go field-set drift can ship green.

Top risks: missing mandated parity tests (cursor ordering, unknown version, subscription tenant shape), undefined observability/config contract names assigned to this item, and no test proving the idempotency-header/event_id invariant.
